arxiv-2207-03634.title: Integrating Sensing, Computing, and Communication in 6G Wireless Networks: Design and Optimization
arxiv-2207-03634.creator: Qiao Qi, Xiaoming Chen, Ata Khalili, Caijun Zhong, Zhaoyang Zhang, Derrick Wing Kwan Ng
arxiv-2207-03634.description: Abstract The roll-out of various emerging wireless services has triggered the need for the sixth-generation (6G) wireless networks to provide functions of target sensing, intelligent computing and information communication over the same radio spectrum. In this paper, we provide a unified framework integrating sensing, computing, and communication to optimize limited system resource for 6G wireless networks.

arxiv-2210-17411.title: Offset-Guided Attention Network for Room-Level Aware Floor Plan Segmentation
arxiv-2210-17411.creator: ZHANGYU WANG 1, NINGYUAN SUN 2
arxiv-2210-17411.description: Abstract Recognition of floor plans has been a challenging and popular task. Despite that many recent approaches have been proposed for this task, they typically fail to make the room-level unified prediction. Specifically, multiple semantic categories can be assigned in a single room, which seriously limits their visual quality and applicability.

arxiv-2305-16767.title: A Viscoelastic Model for Droplet Breakup in Dense Emulsions
arxiv-2305-16767.creator: Joseph D. Peterson, Ioannis Bagkeris, Vipin Michael
arxiv-2305-16767.description: Abstract When processing dense emulsions, complex flows stretch and deform droplets to the point of breakup, changing the droplet size distribution and the mechanical properties of the final product. For steady homogeneous flows, a droplet’s shape and proclivity to breakup can be inferred from a Capillary number, comparing the strain rate with the typical shape relaxation time.

arxiv-2401-04903.title: SnapCap: Efficient Snapshot Compressive Video Captioning
arxiv-2401-04903.creator: Jianqiao Sun, Yudi Su, Hao Zhang*, Ziheng Cheng, Zequn Zeng, Zhengjue Wang, Bo Chen*, Xin Yuan*
arxiv-2401-04903.description: Abstract Video Captioning (VC) is a challenging multi-modal task since it requires describing the scene in language by understanding various and complex videos. For machines, the traditional VC follows the “imaging-compression-decoding-and-then-captioning” pipeline, where compression is pivot for storage and transmission. arxiv-2405-03506.title: Spin-Wave Voices: Sonification of Nanoscale Spin Waves as an Engagement and Research Tool
arxiv-2405-03506.description: Abstract Magnonics is an emerging research field that addresses the use of spin waves (magnons), purely magnetic waves, for information transport and processing. Spin waves are a potential replacement for electric current in novel computational devices that would make them more compact and energy efficient. The field is yet little known, even among physicists.

arxiv-2406-05851.title: Effect of Torsion on Neutron Star Structure in Einstein-Cartan Gravity
arxiv-2406-05851.creator: Cédric Jockel, Leon Menger
arxiv-2406-05851.description: Abstract Einstein–Cartan gravity is a close historical sibling of general relativity that allows for spacetime torsion. As a result, angular momentum couples to spacetime geometry in a similar way to energy. While consequences of this are well studied on cosmological scales, their role in neutron star physics is largely under-explored.

arxiv-2501-18176.title: Experimental asymmetric relativistic zero-knowledge proofs with unconditional security
arxiv-2501-18176.creator: Chen-Xun Weng, Ming-Yang Li, Nai-Rui Xu, Yanglin Hu, Ian George, Jiawei Wu, Shengjun Wu, Hua-Lei Yin, Zeng-Bing Chen
arxiv-2501-18176.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chen-Xun Weng, Ming-Yang Li, Nai-Rui Xu, Yanglin Hu, Ian George, Jiawei Wu, Shengjun Wu, Hua-Lei Yin, Zeng-Bing Chen. Zero-knowledge proofs (ZKPs) are widely applied in digital economies, such as cryptocurrencies and smart contracts, for establishing trust and privacy between untrusted parties. Classical ZKPs rely on computational assumptions and are vulnerable to quantum attacks.

arxiv-2510-02887.title: GramTrans: A Better Code Representation Approach in Code Generation
arxiv-2510-02887.creator: Zhao Zhang, Qingyuan Liang, Zeyu Sun, Yizhou Chen, Guoqing Wang, Yican Sun, Lu Zhang, Ge Li, Yingfei Xiong
arxiv-2510-02887.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Zhao Zhang, Qingyuan Liang, Zeyu Sun, Yizhou Chen, Guoqing Wang, Yican Sun, Lu Zhang, Ge Li, Yingfei Xiong. Code generation has shown great promise in assisting software development. A fundamental yet underexplored question is how the choice of code representation affects model performance. While existing studies employ various representations, such as treating code as plain text, grammar rule sequences, or syntax tree sequences, they lack a principled understanding of the relationship between parsing difficulty and model effectiveness.

pmc-11569163.creator: Sergey Grigoriev, Nikita Nikitin, Oleg Yanushevich, Natella Krikheli, Roman Khmyrov, Daniil Strunevich, Mihail Soloninkin, Nestor Washington Solis Pinargote, Pavel Peretyagin, Anton Smirnov

The task of reducing the amount of material required to manufacture a product without significant loss of mechanical properties is one of the most practically important technological tasks.

pmc-12405554.title: Distinct circulating autoantibodies are associated with COVID-19 hospitalization and SARS-CoV-2 neutralization activity
pmc-12405554.creator: Rajesh Abraham Jacob, Hannah O. Ajoge, Michael R. D’Agostino, Altynay Shigayeva, Arinjay Banerjee, Matthew S. Miller, Allison J. McGeer, Samira Mubareka, Karen Mossman
pmc-12405554.description: SARS-CoV-2 infection disrupts the host’s immune system, altering autoimmune responses. This study investigated host autoreactivities in SARS-CoV-2 infections, their association with severe COVID-19, and the neutralizing antibody response. Circulating autoantibodies were detected in convalescent serum samples from unvaccinated SARS-CoV-2-infected patients.

pmc-12734120.title: Mapping the Genetic Relatedness of Outdoor-Biting Anopheles Mosquitoes in Zambia
pmc-12734120.creator: Reneé L. M. N. Ali, Mary E. Gebhardt, Limonty Simubali, Kochelani Saili, Westone Hamwata, Hunter Chilusu, Mbanga Muleba, Conor J. McMeniman, Anne C. Martin, William J. Moss, Douglas E. Norris
pmc-12734120.description: Simple SummaryOutdoor-biting Anopheles mosquitoes have been gaining attention due to their potential role in sustaining malaria transmission by avoiding indoor vector control interventions. The efficacy of mitigation efforts that primarily target indoor biting and resting mosquitoes may be undermined by these mosquitoes.

pmc-13190558.title: Perceived competence and cognitive bias in nurses' assessment of intimate partner violence: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13190558.creator: David Casero-Benavente, Natalia Mudarra-García, Guillermo Charneco-Salguero, Francisco Lencina-Navarro, Diego Pérez-Iglesias, Cecilia Castillo-Gallardo, Raquel Vázquez-Royo, Paula Panadero-Puente, Francisco Javier García-Sánchez, José Miguel Cárdenas-Rebollo
pmc-13190558.description: IntroductionIntimate partner violence (IPV) represents a complex social and health problem that requires multidisciplinary responses. Healthcare professionals, particularly nurses, play a key role in the identification and management of IPV cases. However, limited training and potential cognitive biases may affect professional assessment and intervention.MethodsA cross-sectional descriptive study was conducted among 202 nursing professionals in Spain.

pmc-13242996.title: Extracellular Vesicle-Based Strategies for the Prevention of Chemotherapy-Induced Cardiotoxicity
pmc-13242996.creator: Zhaoqin Shen, Jie Qiu, Wei Yu, Rumeng Chen, Yuancong Jiang
pmc-13242996.description: Chemotherapy-induced cardiotoxicity (CIC) is a major limitation of modern anticancer therapy, particularly with anthracyclines and targeted agents, and contributes to long-term cardiovascular complications in cancer survivors. Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are nanoscale lipid-bilayer particles that mediate intercellular communication through the transfer of proteins, nucleic acids, and lipids. Emerging evidence indicates that EVs play a dual role in CIC.

pmc-13535021.title: Transient monocular vertical hemifield loss as a rare acute oxaliplatin-induced ophthalmological side effect: a case report and review of the literature
pmc-13535021.creator: Lucie Regaldo-Saint Blancard, Simon Pernot, Marianne Fonck, Lola Jade Palmieri
pmc-13535021.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Oxaliplatin commonly induces acute, transient peripheral neurotoxicity, most often presenting as cold-induced paresthesia. Ocular adverse events are rare and poorly understood. This case describes a rare, reproducible transient monocular visual field loss associated with oxaliplatin exposure. We report a patient treated with FOLFOX (5-FU + oxaliplatin) for metastatic rectal cancer who developed recurrent transient visual symptoms temporally associated with oxaliplatin infusion. Biological, neurological, and ophthalmological evaluations were performed. The patient experienced recurrent, transient left monocular vertical hemifield loss during oxaliplatin administration.

pmc-13566155.title: Is Morning Exposure Therapy More Successful? Pilot Data on Exposure Process Indicators and Diurnal Cortisol in Obsessive–Compulsive Disorder or Agoraphobia
pmc-13566155.creator: Michael Kellner, Maja Santai Mareljic, Alexander Yassouridis
pmc-13566155.description: Background/Objectives: Glucocorticoids have been shown to improve fear extinction learning in preclinical and human studies. We hypothesized an impact of the circadian rhythm of cortisol on exposure therapy in patients with anxiety spectrum disorders. Methods: Sixteen patients suffering from obsessive–compulsive disorder and eight with agoraphobia participated in a pilot randomized prospective cohort study.

uslaw-usc-t28-s2710.title: 28 U.S.C. § 2710 — Right of attachment
uslaw-usc-t28-s2710.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t28-s2710.description: United States Code, Title 28 (Judiciary And Judicial Procedure); Part VI (Particular Proceedings); Chapter 173 (Attachment In Postal Suits). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) Where debts are due from a defaulting or delinquent postmaster, contractor, or other officer, agent or employee of the Post Office Department, a warrant of attachment may issue against all property and legal and equitable rights belonging.
